blocks.text: Why media planners need a better Excel workflow on Mac

Media planning requires precision. You move from client budgets to media buy schedules in minutes. When your Excel file slows down, your strategy suffers. Mac users face unique challenges with Excel. Some Windows shortcuts do not translate directly. Others conflict with macOS system commands. You need to know which settings to change to keep your flow.
Essential Excel keyboard shortcuts for Mac

Stop using your trackpad for everything. Keyboard shortcuts are the fastest way to manipulate campaign data. Use Fn + F2 to edit an active cell instantly. Press Shift + Space to select an entire row. Use Ctrl + Space to select an entire column. If you need to fill data down a column, use Cmd + D. These small habits add up over a long planning cycle.
If a shortcut like Cmd + T does not create a table, check your System Settings. Go to Keyboard > Shortcuts and ensure the Excel command is not blocked by a macOS system hotkey.
blocks.title: Fixing shortcut conflicts

blocks.text: Excel supports up to 1,048,576 rows. That is rarely the problem. The problem is how you organize the data. Avoid blank rows within your dataset. They break filters and pivot tables. Use tables instead of ranges. Select your data and press Cmd + T. This creates a structured table. It makes referencing data in formulas much easier.
The power of XLOOKUP for media data

Forget VLOOKUP. It has limitations that cause errors in complex media plans. It cannot look to the left. It breaks when you insert columns. XLOOKUP is the modern standard for Microsoft 365. It handles exact matches by default. It is faster and more reliable for linking campaign IDs to performance metrics.

items: Storing phone numbers or IDs as numbers. Excel strips leading zeros. Format these columns as Text first.
Hardcoding values in formulas. Use cell references so your plan updates when your budget changes.
Overusing conditional formatting. It slows down large workbooks significantly.
Ignoring error checks. Use IFERROR to keep your reports clean when data is missing.

blocks.text: How to stay organized while planning

Your spreadsheet is only one part of the puzzle. Use Apple Calendar for time blocking your deep work. Use NotePlan to track your status updates. Keep your Excel files in a synced folder like iCloud Drive or OneDrive. This ensures you can access your latest media plan from any device.

faq.question: Why does Excel on Mac feel different from Windows?
faq.answer: Microsoft 365 for Mac is built for macOS. It uses different underlying frameworks. Some advanced features like Power Query are not identical to the Windows version. However, core functions and formulas work the same.

faq.question: Can Lazur help me learn Excel formulas?
faq.answer: Yes. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur to explain a specific formula like XLOOKUP or COUNTIFS. It will walk you through the syntax and how to apply it to your data.

faq.question: How do I speed up a slow Excel file?
faq.answer: Remove unnecessary formatting. Delete hidden objects. Convert ranges to tables. If the file is still slow, try saving it as a binary workbook (.xlsb) to reduce the file size.
